cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Make Help Define Us
cards.instruction: Get their help, then use how it is offered to redefine what the relationship means.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Carry the table with me, not for me. I'd like us to be partners today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm stronger. I can do it alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. That's the arrangement I'm trying to stop calling our friendship.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Take the other end.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Now ask where we're putting it instead of deciding for both ends.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved the soup. You may start lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was asking whether you'd pass the salt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request is under consideration.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll get it myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent initiative. Approved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Welcome to my garage sale. Your offer to browse is accepted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my garage. You're helping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you're doing very well under my supervision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm going inside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Granted. Take five.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me write the complaint as a colleague, not my parent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was only correcting your spelling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then leave the angry sentence. That's my contribution.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's quite a good sentence.

beats.text: Good. Put both our names under it, not 'on behalf of.'

cards.title: Reopen the First Reason
cards.instruction: Keep them present by returning to the first reason for staying and revealing that it now means something different.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Stay until the tea cools. You always rush goodbye.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then I wasn't really waiting for the tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What were you waiting for?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A goodbye that doesn't sound like you're already somewhere else. Have another sip.

cards.title: Change What the Apology Is For
cards.instruction: Get an apology, then reveal that the original offense was only the first layer of what needs repair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Thank you for apologising for missing my concert.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So we're okay?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Closer. Now why did I have to ask whether you'd noticed missing it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't know what to say.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then apologise for letting me rehearse your apology alone all week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved the soup. You may start lunch.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I approved furniture, not a committee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then welcome to our first agenda item: what your chair authorises.

cards.title: The Handoff Already Happened
cards.instruction: Get them to accept responsibility by returning to earlier offers until the task seems to have been assigned all along.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. You said you'd take it from here. Here are the unanswered wedding invitations.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Exactly. These people need an answer before reaching it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's not the same job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then help me explain where your generous offer ended.
